[Updates]{.eyebrow}

Announcements, milestones, meetings, and outputs from the collaboration.

### October 2026 — Review manuscript prepared

A working manuscript, *Mathematical Models of Pollinator Populations: A Multi-Scale Review and Research Agenda for Honey Bees and Beyond*, now synthesises the literature across five thematic pillars, identifies sixteen open mathematical problems and two cross-cutting methodological questions, and connects them to the collaboration's staged research agenda. Authorship and affiliations are still being confirmed, so the document is posted as a working manuscript rather than a final publication. [Download the manuscript](resources/Mathematical-Models-of-Pollinator-Populations-Working-Manuscript-2026.pdf).

### May 2026 — Workshop final report released

The final report of the AIM workshop *Addressing Declining Pollinator Populations Through New Mathematics* synthesises outcomes from all eight working groups and sets out a coordinated twelve-month research and partnership roadmap. [Download the final report](resources/AIM-Workshop-Final-Report-2026.pdf).

### April 2026 — Workshop concludes at AIM

The workshop ran March 30 – April 5, 2026, convening mathematicians, ecologists, data scientists, and commercial beekeeping practitioners. Eight working groups produced the six priority research directions that now define the collaboration's agenda.

### In progress — Shared research infrastructure

Work continues on the dataset crosswalk, sub-team formation around the six priority areas, and power analysis for a future large-scale monitoring study.
